To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we experimentally demonstrated optical information processing using an optoelectronics oscillator subject to delayed feed-back.

we experimentally implement an unconventional computational paradigm based on a complex dynamical systems approach to information processing, and that we demonstrate its potential in the context of two information processing tasks, spoken digit recognition and chaotic time series prediction.

we demonstrate the use of nonlinear optoelectronics as a platform for implementing a reservoir computer, a novel approach to information processing that has been shown to possess universal computational power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implementation of unconventional computational methods using optical systems.
the design of novel photonic information processing architectures and the implementation of unconventional computational methods in optical systems.
the development of novel optical computing paradigms, and the implementation of such paradigms in optoelectronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work demonstrates that a nonlinear optoeletronics system is capable of performing information processing tasks that are beyond the reach of conventional Turing or von Neuman approaches.
this paper is the first to experimentally demonstrate the implementation of a Reservoir Computing architecture based on a photonic system.
the proposed optoelectronic system is a promising platform for implementing reservoir computing, a neuro-inspired information processing paradigm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate a new approach for optical computing, which is based on nonlinear dynamics, and which can be applied to a broad range of information processing tasks.

we experimentally implement a reservoir computing system using a nonlinear opto-electronic oscillator subject to feedback and we demonstrate the capability of such a system to solve complex computational tasks.
a nonlinear optoelectric circuit can perform a complex computational task with the same efficiency as a state-of-the-art digital computer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optoelectronic approach to Reservoir Computing is a promising candidate for the implementation of a wide range of unconventional information processing tasks.
unconventional computational methods can be efficiently implemented using optical components.
optical systems are able to perform information processing tasks that are beyond Turing and that can be implemented in a compact and efficient fashion.
